finalists.text:
After the session Mara came out to a warm night, dry except for the smell of wet moss under the trees. Jonah was on the front steps beside a black pickup.

Mara turned as he closed the door. “I’ll walk home.”

“Okay.” The low voice didn’t ask for explanations.

Jonah closed his hand on the door’s metal bar and rested beside it. When she stood straight and met his eyes he offered a hand, palm up, wrist steady. His eyes said “I wait for you.”

Mara set her left hand in his and let their fingertips touch without squeezing. He held it with just enough pressure to balance her if she moved. His back straightened and the muscles around his eyes eased as if he’d just taken an easy breath.

A full breath took too much attention so Mara looked at their feet and moved hers under the truck’s bumper. Jonah put his right hand behind him on the step above and waited for her to move.

She tried a small step off the front porch. He let their joined hands stay steady without pushing against her. When she said, “Okay,” they walked.

Jonah took a wider step, moving her hand with the easy strength of his stride. After three steps Mara let the heel of her free hand rest on his elbow. She was used to holding someone when they walked. Jonah’s arm wasn’t tight, and he let her use his elbow without changing his pace or direction.

The walk took Mara through a part of herself she kept closed in the lab. When Jonah turned to look at her she let her hand slide higher on his sleeve to let them see each other more clearly. She watched his eyes follow the change. He said nothing while she moved her hand to rest between his arm and side.

When he looked forward again he took a wider step, then slowed his pace so Mara could move next to him. When she said nothing for a long time Jonah finally asked, “Why did you do it?”

“Do what?”

Jonah glanced over so the question was more of a look. “Stop them.”

“Why not? They’re hurting people. I won’t let people I care about get hurt.”

He didn’t argue with her. They reached the sidewalk in the street and Mara let her left hand fall from his to her side. She stood alone while Jonah unlocked the truck door, then watched as he put his keys on the front seat and shut the door again. When he turned to face her she knew exactly what he was going to ask.

“Can I offer you a ride?” The voice was steady.

“I’ll walk, thanks. I can walk to my own apartment.”

Mara didn’t expect an argument and didn’t get one. After two steps Mara said, “Can we just walk for a while? Can we be alone?”

He turned so they could meet his eyes. She waited to see what he would say.

“Yes.”

She took his offered hand and he let them walk slowly. After four steps she said, “I want to stop for a moment and put my forehead against yours so we can just breathe together.”

He stopped at the corner and turned to face her, then closed one eye. Mara moved to him and lifted their joined hands to his chest to stand steady. Jonah kept his voice low. “I’m breathing for both of us right now.”

Mara put her forehead against his while Jonah’s other hand went slowly to hold her arm. She was quiet until she heard the distant sound of traffic, then finally looked up. “What about a kiss?”

“If you want one.”

Mara pulled a quick breath and closed her eyes. “I think I want one. We’ll see.”

Jonah moved toward her with their hands joined, his hand moving to her right waist. He touched her gently and waited. Mara moved the hand holding him and put it on his chest. She felt him pause an instant before saying, “This is what you want?”

She opened her eyes to meet his, then closed them again. He slid his other hand along the back of her head until she could feel fingers lightly moving hair away from her neck. His hand went slowly to the back of her neck as their faces came closer. Mara touched his cheek and neck with her own fingers as he leaned closer. She met him halfway, then lifted her right hand to hold the back of his neck.

Mara felt their lips join before they moved together, then tried a slow kiss and broke it for a moment. He held her steady and breathed quietly while she closed her eyes. The kiss was strong and warm and moved from her lips through her shoulders without hurting. She was surprised when the sound of Jonah’s slow breath finally let her feel herself again.

“Wait,” she said. “Just a minute.”

Jonah released her shoulders, then let their joined hands fall to his waist as he waited for her to speak. Mara caught her breath in time to hear a car turn the corner.

“It was good.”

He said nothing, just waited with his eyes steady. Mara tried another short kiss, then let go of Jonah’s neck. He took a full step back and turned to look in the direction she had been walking. The street was empty except for distant lights.

“That’s my turn.” Mara opened her eyes to meet Jonah’s steady gaze. He waited without asking if she wanted to continue. Mara saw how he was letting them make each choice as a new step.

Mara moved her hands from his shirt and dropped their joined hands. She pulled a full breath and closed her eyes again. “That was good. Thank you.”

Jonah said nothing when she turned away, but his pace told Mara he was staying near as she reached the cross street. When Mara moved past the trees under an arc light she stopped and turned to him. He let his hand rest on his truck’s hood as she started to speak.

Mara waited to hear his words, but only heard the sound of a distant train. The moment took her breath for an instant while she looked into Jonah’s eyes. “I wish it were later. I wish we were alone.”

Jonah stepped away from the truck and walked toward her without hurrying. He held her upper arms in both hands for a moment, then let go to rest his hand on her waist while he spoke. “Me, too. And I’m sorry that I couldn’t be there before it happened.”

Mara had known he would say something like that. She tried another kiss and held on to his shirt as she felt his hands touch her hips. “When can we meet again?”

He let go of her gently, then turned his face away. Mara followed him with a question in her voice while Jonah unlocked the truck and opened the door. He waited while she stood in the street. Mara said, “I can walk the rest of the way.”

Jonah said nothing while he sat in the truck, then reached out the window for her hand. “I want to come see you tomorrow. Can I bring my notebook?”

Mara looked up at him with a question in her eyes. “You want me to read it?”

His hands dropped the window again while he said, “I’d be proud if you did.”

Mara let him drop her hand when she answered, “Yes. You can come tomorrow.”

Jonah took her hand for one quick kiss, then closed the window as the engine started. The truck moved slowly through the intersection and kept going while Mara watched it go. She stood alone in the street under the lights, feeling the sudden change.

When Mara let her eyes close she felt herself stand alone at the edge of the woods.

A single light showed the road and the open space around her, but behind her only the dark trees filled the sky. The sound of traffic still told her she was far from any open field, yet the instant brought a sudden fear that made her heart race.

“I don’t want to be alone.” The words came out as an almost-scream in the night air. The noise frightened her, and Mara let out an even louder scream. A car went by and she felt a flash of cold while she stood in the road. She forced herself to go back to the sidewalk.

Mara stopped after four steps and tried to find a steady thought. Her breath came fast and she made herself take three deep breaths through her nose. When she heard a second car pass she opened her eyes to a view of the empty street.

“I’m here, I’m safe,” Mara told herself aloud. “I’m not alone, and I’ll be there again.” The words were steady and her breath slowed to normal.

Mara went down the street in the direction Jonah’s truck had gone, taking one slow step at a time. She made herself look straight ahead, then stopped again when she saw the next corner.

“What if he’s just using me?” She spoke aloud to hear what she couldn’t say inside herself. “What if I only exist for him as something he’ll throw away when he’s done?”

The fear came back and Mara said it aloud so she could hear it clearly. “What if he’s another man who will just use my body and then leave me? What if I only mean what he can have for himself tonight?”

A second car turned the corner and Mara stopped while it passed, then spoke again. “That’s not who he is. He doesn’t treat me that way, and he never has. He won’t take anything I don’t freely give him.”

Mara tried to find a clear thought and repeated herself as if she were telling someone else what to do. “I’m fine. I’m safe, and he is not going to hurt me. I choose to stay alone with him tomorrow and we will be together willingly.”

Mara tried to remember the touch of their joined hands and the feel of a real kiss. When she could make her body still she let herself take three deep breaths. “I’m fine,” she said again. “And I’ll be there when he comes.”
